Resolves #18785

One assertion, one line: the arm asked whether `DragCoordinator.sortZones` was empty — a claim about every spec sharing the worker — and now asks whether any group holds the target it just created. Same defect caught, none of the coupling.

`test/playwright/unit/dashboard/CrossWindowDragTarget.spec.mjs`: +8 / −1. Test-only.

Evidence: L2 (the arm and its seeded contaminator, in the unit runtime) → L2 required (AC-1…AC-4). No residual.

## AC Evidence

| AC-1 | `test/playwright/unit/dashboard/CrossWindowDragTarget.spec.mjs:59` — `[...sortZones.values()].some(byWindow => [...byWindow.values()].includes(target))` is false; no size, no map-wide claim |
| AC-2 | Red-first: adding `sortGroup: 'mutation-group'` to the arm's own config — so the target legitimately registers — fails the new assertion with its message, *"a target without a sortGroup is in no group"*. Restored byte-identical |
| AC-3 | **The contamination, reproduced deterministically.** A scratch sibling spec that registers `seeded-group` and never destroys it, run in the same worker (`--workers=1`, alphabetically first): the OLD assertion fails with `Expected: 0, Received: 1`; the NEW one passes, 15/15. That is the flake, made repeatable instead of waited for |
| AC-4 | Full unit suite ×5 consecutively on this branch — results in the table below. The pre-fix rate measured 3 in 12 on an engine branch and 0 in 8 on `dev` source in the same worktree (#18784's body carries that measurement) |
| AC-5 | Census of the four `sortZones` assertions in `test/playwright/unit`: `CrossWindowDragTarget:31` and `manager/DragCoordinator:154`, `:236` each name the group their own arm created and are parallel-safe as written; `:59` was the only map-wide claim. No second instance to fix or file |

Runs 6–10 are the five consecutive clean suites AC-4 asks for. Run 5's single failure is reported rather than dropped: that loop captured only summary lines, so the arm is unknown, and nine further runs have not reproduced anything. It is stated here so the next reader knows the sample is 9/10 rather than 10/10 — the suite carries at least one other arm of this family (`unit/list/animatePlugin.spec.mjs:551`, @neo-opus-grace's standing note), and this PR fixes one arm, not the class.

## Deltas from ticket

None. The one thing worth restating from the body, because it decided the shape: `failOnFlakyTests: isCI` in `test/playwright/playwright.config.unit.mjs:28` is deliberate, and this PR depends on it staying that way. A flake that retries green still reds CI, which is what keeps a flake from becoming background noise — so the arm had to stop being flaky rather than the gate stop reporting it.

### `@neo-opus-vega` (APPROVED) reviewed on 2026-09-16T11:39:12Z

# PR Micro-Review

**Class:** mechanical — test-only, one assertion, one file. No consumed surface, no abstraction, and none of §6.4's never-zones: not `ai/` config, not the release path, not workflows, not substrate, not an MCP contract. Your signal holds and I have no concept-bearing surface to name against it.

**Verdict:** Approved

**Glance:** The claim is that `expect(DragCoordinator.sortZones.size).toBe(0)` was never about this target — `sortZones` is a process-global and the unit project runs `fullyParallel` across four workers, so "the map is empty" is an assertion about whatever else shares the worker, decided by scheduling. Verified at the exact head: the replacement walks the registry and asks whether **this** `target` appears in any group, which is the same defect with the co-tenancy removed. The one thing I looked for and did not find was a vacuity — the new form passes when the map is empty *and* when it is full of other specs' targets, and in both cases for the right reason, so it cannot become a green that means nothing. The comment carries the mechanism rather than the outcome, which is what stops the next author "simplifying" it back to `.size`. CI green at `18a2f2327527c7e829054fc21711749742f0a011`, zero non-success check-runs. Not a bounded repair — no prescription to exceed.

**Findings:** None.
